title: POC: workload nonstationary QPS + token-mix scoping - LumenPath
summary: Kickoff scoping for a POC to characterize nonstationary traffic patterns, QPS bursts, and token mix across LumenPath's chat+search product. Agreed success criteria: 99th percentile tail latency < 450ms for short chats, cost per 1k tokens target, and documented capacity plan for private VPC deployment.
next_steps: Redwood to share benchmark template and sample workload recorder by 2028-03-24
LumenPath to export 2 weeks of anonymized request logs by 2028-03-28
Schedule in-person runbook review with Infra (Elena) week of 2028-04-02
action_items: Maya Chen: send benchmark template + S3 upload instructions - due 2028-03-24
Priya Natarajan: generate anonymized token histogram and sample prompt set - due 2028-03-28
Alonzo Park: draft preliminary topology for dedicated GPU pool and fallback routing - due 2028-03-30
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then jump into traffic shape.
[00:12] Rashid Ahmed: Hey, Rashid here, platform. We run a hybrid chat/search stack, little bit of rerank. Main concern is bursty QPS during promo windows.
[00:25] Alonzo Park: Great thanks. I want to understand the nonstationary bits — are bursts regular or random?
[00:33] Priya Natarajan: Mostly predictable, like marketing pushes and new feature launches, but we've also seen weird tails from notification storms. Concurrency can spike from 50 to 1200 in a minute.
[00:45] Maya Chen: Okay, that variance matters for batching and tail latency. Can you give us typical request sizes? tokens in/out?
[00:55] Priya Natarajan: Avg input prompt ~40 tokens, but we have long-context flows up to 2k tokens for conversation history; output average 28 tokens, but in certain fallback cases up to 600 tokens.
[01:07] Elena Morales: To add, we keep a 30-day conversation history in our DB but only send last 3 messages; we might switch to sending a summary which changes token distributions.
[01:20] Alonzo Park: That helps. For POC we'll want a token mix distribution: short chat (70%), short search rerank (20%), long-context debug flows (10%). Does that sound right?
[01:32] Priya Natarajan: Yes, approximately. Also our QPS baseline is around 120 qps globally, but bursts go to 1.5k qps across regions, usually lasting 3-10 minutes.
[01:45] Maya Chen: Good. Success criteria — let's propose: 95th < 200ms for short chats, 99th < 450ms, and throughput sufficient to cover 1.5k qps with the observed token mix while keeping per-1k-token cost under your target.
[01:58] Rashid Ahmed: Cost is important — we have a target of under $0.80 per 1k effective tokens for production. Also, security: must be VPC private control plane, KMS for keys, SOC 2 logs.
[02:12] Maya Chen: Redwood Private supports that; we'll include the security pack and a compliance doc. Alonzo, can you sketch a benchmark plan?
[02:20] Alonzo Park: Sure. Phase 1: ingest anonymized logs and synthesize workload replay (QPS timeline + token histograms). Phase 2: run controlled concurrency sweep on Redwood Dedicated + fallback to hosted to measure degradation points. Phase 3: tail-latency profiling and KV cache checksum for long-context. We'll collect p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, tokens/sec, and cost model outputs.
[02:41] Priya Natarajan: For replay— we need a mode to preserve burstiness and diurnal shifts, not just averaged QPS.
[02:49] Alonzo Park: Agreed — we'll use a nonstationary generator that replays real inter-arrival times so we capture queueing effects.
[02:55] Elena Morales: Networking question — we have private subnets in GCP and an on-prem DR site. Can Redwood Dedicated sit in our VPC peered fashion?
[03:06] Jordan Li: We support VPC peering and private deployment; for on-prem we'd do a hybrid tunnel. We'll note bandwidth and NAT translation requirements in the runbook.
[03:18] Gabe Torres: Any limitations on model length and quantization? We plan to test 13B and 70B family quantized to 4-bit.
[03:28] Alonzo Park: We support quantized paths; kernel selection changes with sequence length. For 70B at 4-bit you trade latency vs cost — we should include a model variant matrix in the benchmark.
[03:40] Rashid Ahmed: Also fallback strategy — if dedicated pool saturated, we need deterministic fallback to a slightly cheaper hosted variant. Can Redwood do automated routing?
[03:50] Maya Chen: Yes, policy-based routing with per-request tiers. We'll simulate failover during Phase 2.
[03:57] Priya Natarajan: Timeline — we want a 6-week POC: week 0-1 log handoff & prep, week 2 replay + baseline runs, week 3-4 scaling experiments, week 5 acceptance benchmarks, week 6 handoff & SOW negotiation. Is that feasible?
[04:12] Alonzo Park: That seems reasonable. If logs arrive on time we can start replay in 48 hours and spin up dedicated infra in 72 hours.
[04:20] Elena Morales: On the logs — we need a template to scrub PII and instructions for rate-limited S3 upload.
[04:27] Maya Chen: We'll send the template and a small python scrubber snippet.
[04:32] Priya Natarajan: For success criteria acceptance, we need a runbook that defines the exact queries and thresholds.
[04:38] Maya Chen: We'll attach the runbook and the exact scenario definitions to the acceptance criteria doc.
[04:43] Rashid Ahmed: One more thing — audit logs retention. We need 90-day immutability for compliance.
[04:49] Jordan Li: Redwood Console supports configurable retention; we'll surface the options and any storage cost impact.
[04:55] Gabe Torres: Competitors — we've benchmarked two other vendors; we want to make sure your tests are apples-to-apples.
[05:01] Maya Chen: We'll include our exact payloads and measurement scripts so you can reproduce vendor comparisons.
[05:07] Alonzo Park: Technical knobs we'll measure: batching window, KV cache hit rate, sequence-length based kernel selection, and quantization profile. We'll collect traces and perf counters.
[05:18] Priya Natarajan: When you talk about KV cache — how do you handle conversation cache invalidation? We sometimes see stale context when users change intent.
[05:26] Alonzo Park: We'll walk through TTL strategies and per-conversation versioning; for the POC we'll instrument invalidation counters.
[05:34] Maya Chen: Ok let's recap action items. Maya sends template + security docs. Priya produces anonymized histograms. Alonzo provides topology and preliminary cost model. We'll aim to have the first replay run by 2028-03-29.
[05:48] Rashid Ahmed: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[05:51] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the runbook deep-dive.
[05:55] [call ends]
